Integrated machine learning for multi-omics multiclass classification

Source: R/IL_multiclass.R
IL_multiclass.Rd

Native multiclass backend used by IntegratedLearner() when family = binomial() and the outcome has more than two classes. This backend preserves the existing API while using multiclass-native probability modeling and multiclass stacking.

Usage

IL_multiclass(
  feature_table,
  sample_metadata,
  feature_metadata,
  feature_table_valid = NULL,
  sample_metadata_valid = NULL,
  folds = 5,
  base_learner = "glmnet",
  base_screener = "All",
  run_screening = FALSE,
  screen_pct = NULL,
  filter_method = NULL,
  filter_pct = NULL,
  prevalence_pct = NULL,
  meta_learner = "glmnet",
  run_concat = TRUE,
  run_stacked = TRUE,
  run_intermediate = FALSE,
  cooperative_rho = c(0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1),
  cooperative_s = "lambda.min",
  cooperative_type_measure = NULL,
  family = stats::binomial(),
  eps = 1e-15,
  run_majority = TRUE,
  run_weighted = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

feature_table

An R data frame containing multi-layer features (in rows) and samples (in columns). Column names of feature_metadata must match the row names of sample_metadata.

sample_metadata

An R data frame of metadata variables (in columns). Must have a column named subjectID describing per-subject unique identifiers. For longitudinal designs, this variable may be non-unique. Additionally, a column named Y must be present which is the continuous or binary outcome of interest. Row names of sample_metadata must match the column names of feature_table.

feature_metadata

An R data frame of feature-specific metadata across views (in columns) and features (in rows). Must have a column named featureID as a unique per-feature identifier and a column named featureType describing the source layers. Row names of feature_metadata must match the row names of feature_table.

feature_table_valid

Feature table from validation set for which prediction is desired. Must have the exact same structure as feature_table. If missing, uses feature_table.

sample_metadata_valid

Sample-specific metadata table from independent validation set when available. Must have the exact same structure as sample_metadata.

folds

Number of subject-level folds for out-of-fold predictions. Default 5. Fully nested evaluation of the fusion pipeline is separate.

base_learner

Native multiclass base learner. Default "glmnet".

base_screener

Deprecated for this backend; currently ignored and kept only for backward compatibility.

run_screening

Logical; if TRUE, run supervised screening within each training fold (and again on full training data) before fitting base models.

screen_pct

Percentage of features to retain during screening ((0,100]). Applied after any optional filtering.

filter_method

Optional feature-filter method before model fitting. Supported values are 'prevalence' (top detected features by prevalence) and 'variance' (top features by caret-based variance ranking via nearZeroVar + empirical variance). If NULL, defaults to 'prevalence' when filtering is requested.

filter_pct

Optional retention percentage (in (0,100]) for the selected filter_method. Keeps the top filter_pct percent features.

prevalence_pct

Optional retention percentage (in (0,100]) for prevalence-based filtering before model fitting. Deprecated alias of filter_pct with filter_method = 'prevalence'.

meta_learner

Native multiclass stacking learner. Default "glmnet". Legacy sl_nnls_auc and SL.nnls aliases map to multinomial glmnet, not scalar layer-weight optimization.

run_concat

Should early fusion be run? Default is TRUE.

run_stacked

Should stacked model (late fusion) be run? Default is TRUE.

run_intermediate

Ignored for multiclass outcomes with a message; cooperative multiview learning is not currently supported for multiclass fits.

cooperative_rho

Non-negative agreement-penalty values to evaluate for cooperative learning.

cooperative_s

Penalty value used when predicting from the selected cooperative model. Defaults to "lambda.min".

cooperative_type_measure

Optional multiview CV loss/score. If NULL, an outcome-appropriate default is used.

family

Allows gaussian() for continuous and binomial() for binary outcomes. Survival outcomes must be handled via IL_survival().

eps

Small positive constant used to stabilize probabilities.

run_majority

Logical; return multiclass majority voting. Default TRUE; ignored for other outcomes. Ties use the first class in training class order.

run_weighted

Logical; return multiclass probability averaging with nonnegative layer weights summing to one, learned by minimizing out-of-fold multiclass log loss. Default TRUE; ignored for other outcomes.

...

Additional arguments passed to native base-model fitting; these are not passed to the stacked meta-model or fusion-weight optimizer.

Value

A fitted multiclass IntegratedLearner object containing class probabilities, predicted classes, fitted single-layer and fusion models, and training/validation multiclass performance summaries when available.

Details

Majority voting returns vote fractions under majority; these are not calibrated class probabilities. Ties use the first class in training class order. Learned averaging returns probabilities under weighted_average and stores final layer weights under model_fits$model_weighted$weights. Weights minimize multiclass log loss on out-of-fold layer probabilities. Training outputs cross-fit the weights across the existing folds. As with stacking, fully nested evaluation is needed for an unbiased assessment of the entire fitted pipeline. Results are also grouped under train_out and valid_out, each with single, early, and late entries. The late list contains all enabled methods: stacked, majority, and weighted_average. Each method includes split-specific probabilities, classes, and metrics; learned averaging also includes final weights and, for training, the weights fitted outside each fold. Existing flat outputs remain available. late_methods lists the returned late-fusion methods. Fusion entries contain train_prob, train_class, a metrics table, and scalar train_accuracy, train_balanced_accuracy, train_auc, and train_logloss; validation entries use the corresponding valid_ names. AUC is the macro average of available one-vs-rest class AUCs. Single-layer entries contain probability lists and class data frames. Without validation data, valid_out is NULL. Disabled early fusion gives early = NULL, and disabled late methods are omitted from late.

Feature importance retains a univariate class-association calculation: for each feature and class, the mean in the remaining classes is subtracted from the mean in that class and divided by the feature's overall training standard deviation plus 1e-8. The signed scores form a feature-by-class matrix in feature_importance_signed_by_class. feature_importance_signed_by_layer_by_class groups these matrices by omics layer and ranks features by mean absolute score across classes. feature_importance_global is the unsigned mean absolute score across classes, ranked highest first. These associations use the training features after optional filtering, including features excluded by screening; they are shared across fusion methods and are not model-specific attributions.

Progress, summaries, and reproducibility

Call set.seed() before fitting to reproduce the data splits and stochastic fitting steps. To display progress, wrap the call in progressr::with_progress(). Use print(fit) to show a fitted model summary.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 24
feature_table <- as.data.frame(rbind(
  matrix(rnorm(3 * n), nrow = 3, dimnames = list(paste0("L1_F", 1:3), paste0("S", 1:n))),
  matrix(rnorm(2 * n), nrow = 2, dimnames = list(paste0("L2_F", 1:2), paste0("S", 1:n)))
))
y <- rep(c("A", "B", "C"), length.out = n)
sample_metadata <- data.frame(
  subjectID = paste0("ID", 1:n), Y = y,
  row.names = colnames(feature_table)
)
feature_metadata <- data.frame(
  featureID = rownames(feature_table),
  featureType = c(rep("Layer1", 3), rep("Layer2", 2)),
  row.names = rownames(feature_table)
)
fit <- IL_multiclass(
  feature_table = feature_table,
  sample_metadata = sample_metadata,
  feature_metadata = feature_metadata,
  folds = 3, base_learner = "multinom", meta_learner = "multinom",
  run_stacked = FALSE, run_concat = FALSE
)
fit$family
#> [1] "multinomial"
fit$late_methods
#> [1] "majority"         "weighted_average"
fit$train_out$late$weighted_average$weights
#>    Layer1    Layer2 
#> 0.2901878 0.7098122 
head(fit$feature_importance_signed_by_layer_by_class[[1]])
#>                A          B          C
#> L1_F1 -0.5194429 -0.1502983  0.6697412
#> L1_F3  0.5698738 -0.3140530 -0.2558207
#> L1_F2  0.3711250 -0.1626989 -0.2084261
